(6) Serialization keeps upstream's dynamic discovery (so any new *Config class is picked up) via the SecureJar root path, with the prior port's explicit list only as a logged fallback. - VoxyRenderSystem: `Viewport<?> setupViewport(Matrix4fc vanillaProjection, Matrix4fc modelView, VoxyFogParameters fog, int width, int height, double cameraX, double cameraY, double cameraZ)`; `void renderOpaque(Viewport<?> viewport, int sourceDepthTexture, int sourceColourTexture)` (throws IllegalStateException if depth tex is 0, as dev); `static int[] getBoundFramebufferTextures()` -> {depthTex, colourTex, width, height} of the currently bound DRAW framebuffer (OBJECT_TYPE must be GL_TEXTURE; if fb 0 / no texture attachment -> Minecraft.getMainRenderTarget() depth/colour/width/height with a one-time warning; throws if there is no depth texture at all); `Viewport<?> getViewport()` (null while the Iris shadow pass is active); `static float getVanillaRenderDistance()`.
- VoxyFogParameters (record environmentalStart, environmentalEnd, red, green, blue, alpha): `of(start,end,float[] rgba)`, `current()`, `lastTerrainFog()`, `setLastTerrainFog()`, `NO_FOG_DISTANCE`, `hasFog()`.

FOG DESIGN (C2) - implemented as VoxyFogEvents (NeoForge ViewportEvent.RenderFog subscriber, priority LOWEST, receiveCanceled=true) rather than a FogRenderer mixin: the event is posted at the end of FogRenderer.setupFog with the vanilla-computed start/end and ClientHooks.onFogRender applies the event values only when cancelled (ref FogRenderer.java:275, ClientHooks.java:447-459); Sodium 0.8.13's FogRendererMixin only redirects the colour sampler in setupColor and Iris 1.8.14's MixinFogRenderer only records water density / fog colour, so nothing fights the event; the prior port used the same event (VoxyClientEvents.onRenderFog). Mapping of 26.2's two fogs onto 1.21.1's single range: the normal FOG_TERRAIN fog is `start = far - clamp(far/10,4,64), end = far` with far = max(gameRenderer.getRenderDistance(),32) (ref FogRenderer.java:266-270, LevelRenderer.java:966) = the render-distance fog WALL (dev always pushes this away); thick fog (isFoggyAt/boss: start=far*0.05,end=min(far,192)*0.5, ref :258-260), mob-effect fogs (:243-248) and fluid fogs end closer = 26.2's ENVIRONMENTAL fog. Handler: only FOG_TERRAIN; capture VoxyFogParameters.of(start,end,RenderSystem.getShaderFogColor()) into lastTerrainFog(); return if !VoxyConfig.CONFIG.isRenderingEnabled() or no render system; return if camera fluid != FogType.NONE (Roxy rule); isRenderDistanceFog = end >= max(renderer.getRenderDistance(),32); fogIsDamnClose = end < 10 (dev rule); push (start=end=1.0E9F like Roxy, then setCanceled(true)) when isRenderDistanceFog || (mode.removesVanillaEnvFog && !fogIsDamnClose). What each FogMode does on 1.21.1: FOG_AND_FADE (dev default): wall removed, thick/effect fog kept, LOD fog = current() (no fog in the overworld since the wall is gone; in kept thick fog NormalRenderPipeline's fogCoversAllRendering skips the LOD blit exactly like dev), LOD alpha fade at 90-100% of the Voxy render distance. FOG: same without the fade. FADE: wall AND thick/effect fog (end>=10) removed, no LOD fog, edge fade. OFF: everything removed (this equals the Roxy 0.3.0 proven baseline `useEnvironmentalFog=false`), no fade. G5 passing VoxyFogParameters.current() at CUTOUT time is correct because dev's Sodium FogParameters were also derived AFTER MixinFogRenderer modified FogData (the pushed 99999999 values), so hasFog only ever saw the untouched environmental fog. Default fogMode stays dev's FOG_AND_FADE: in the overworld it produces the same picture as the Roxy baseline (no wall, no LOD fog) plus the LOD edge fade, and keeps vanilla's thick nether/boss fog; the user's current voxy-config.json has use_environmental_fog=true (so Roxy was in fact NOT pushing the fog for them) and no fogMode key, so no G1 change is requested.

PROJECTION (computeProjectionMat): result = rawProj' * inverse(rawProj) * base with rawProj' = rawProj with m22/m32 replaced by the Voxy near/far (near 8 or 16 by vanilla RD, far 16*3000; reverse-Z/zero-to-one branches kept but inert). For a perspective P = [a 0 0 0; 0 b 0 0; 0 0 c d; 0 0 -1 0], P'*P^-1 = [a'/a 0 0 0; 0 b'/b 0 0; 0 0 d'/d c*d'/d-c'; 0 0 0 1]; with a'=a, b'=b the x/y block is identity, so the matrix depends only on (c,d,c',d') = the near/far planes, and it commutes with the zoom translate/scale GameRenderer may pre-multiply (they act on x/y only). rawProj is therefore rebuilt with GameRenderer.getProjectionMatrix(double) (public, ref GameRenderer.java:980) using the fov OPTION; the effective fov (private getFov, AT-opened in the prior port) is mathematically unnecessary, so no AT line / invoker was added. `base` is Sodium's ChunkRenderMatrices.projection() == RenderSystem.getProjectionMatrix() == rawProj * bobPose (ref GameRenderer.java:1249-1272, Sodium ChunkRenderMatrices.java:11), so the result is rawProj' * bobPose exactly as in dev/upstream 12111.
